prompt: Card.java is provided and complete. Finish Deck.java so its constructor builds all 52 cards in order (suits clubs, diamonds, hearts, spades, each with ranks 1-13), then implement size(), deal(), and contains(rank, suit).
explanation: The Deck class shows one class managing many instances of another: the constructor uses nested loops to create the 52 Card objects, and every later operation works over that stored list. deal() mutates state by removing from the front of the list, so size() shrinks and contains() reflects only the cards still held. Returning null from deal() on an empty deck is a common way to signal "nothing left" without throwing an exception.
hints: Store the cards in an ArrayList<Card> field. In the constructor, loop over a String[] of the four suits, and inside that loop count rank from 1 to 13.
deal() can use cards.remove(0) to take the top card, but check isEmpty() first and return null.
contains needs a loop that compares both getRank() with == and getSuit() with .equals -- remember == is wrong for Strings.
